deck.title: Global Patterns of Energy Supply & Demand

front_blocks.md: Why do some areas of the world produce very little energy?

back_blocks.md: Because they **lack natural resources**, or they do not have the **money to exploit** the resources they have.

back_blocks.md: The world's **largest producers** of energy are often also the **largest consumers** of energy.

Global energy demand is falling as countries develop.

back_blocks.md: **False.**

front_blocks.md: Define **energy surplus**.

back_blocks.md: An **energy surplus** is when a country has more energy sources than it needs.

front_blocks.md: Define **energy deficit**.

back_blocks.md: An **energy deficit** is when a country has a **shortfall** of energy sources and must rely on **trade and imports** to make it up.

front_blocks.md: Name the **four factors** that energy production depends on.

back_blocks.md: **Physical** factors (e.g. geology), **technology**, **economic** factors (price and cost of extraction), and **political** factors (e.g. environmental agendas and wars).

front_blocks.md: Give **three characteristics** of countries that tend to have an energy surplus.

back_blocks.md: **Large reserves of fossil fuels** (e.g. Middle East, Russia), good **access to renewable energy** (e.g. Norway), and a **small population** compared to energy sources available (e.g. Australia).

cards.front_md: Give **three characteristics** of countries that tend to have an energy surplus.
cards.back_md: **Large reserves of fossil fuels** (e.g. Middle East, Russia), good **access to renewable energy** (e.g. Norway), and a **small population** compared to energy sources available (e.g. Australia).

front_blocks.md: Why does **Nepal** tend to have an energy deficit?

front_blocks.md: Define **energy gap**.

back_blocks.md: An **energy gap** is when a country cannot meet its demand for energy using its own resources, so it must **import** energy.

front_blocks.md: What three things does a country need to be **energy secure**?

back_blocks.md: An **uninterrupted** supply, an **affordable** supply, and an **accessible** supply of energy.

cards.front_md: What three things does a country need to be **energy secure**?
cards.back_md: An **uninterrupted** supply, an **affordable** supply, and an **accessible** supply of energy.

front_blocks.md: Give **two reasons** why the UK is not energy secure.

back_blocks.md: **Renewable energy is not efficient enough** to replace fossil fuels, and it is **cheaper to import fossil fuels** than to exploit UK resources.

cards.front_md: Give **two reasons** why the UK is not energy secure.
cards.back_md: **Renewable energy is not efficient enough** to replace fossil fuels, and it is **cheaper to import fossil fuels** than to exploit UK resources.

back_blocks.md: Any three of: **war/conflict**, **natural hazards**, **political disputes**, **cost**, and **environmental concerns**.

front_blocks.md: How does **level of development** lead to low energy consumption in LICs?

back_blocks.md: People **cannot afford** energy, more live a **subsistence farming** lifestyle, and there is **limited access to technology and appliances**, especially in rural areas.

cards.front_md: How does **level of development** lead to low energy consumption in LICs?

front_blocks.md: How does **poor infrastructure** cause low energy consumption in many LICs?

back_blocks.md: Electricity grids are **small, unreliable and don't cover many rural areas**, and gas pipelines and fuel stations may be limited.

back_blocks.md: Any three of: **higher population density**, **better access to energy infrastructure**, **more transport**, and higher energy use for **heating/cooling, entertainment and industries**.
